subtopics.title: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock

questions.questionFamily: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.subtopic: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.question: Explain how fractional distillation separates crude oil and why fractions contain several hydrocarbons rather than one compound.
questions.modelAnswer: Heat/vaporise crude oil; temperature gradient hot bottom/cool top; vapours condense at different heights according to boiling range; drain fractions. Hydrocarbons have similar boiling points, so each fraction is a mixture.
markingPoints: Heat/vaporise crude oil
temperature gradient hot bottom/cool top
vapours condense at different heights according to boiling range
drain fractions. Hydrocarbons have similar boiling points, so each fraction is a mixture.

questions.questionFamily: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.subtopic: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.question: Explain the trends in boiling point, viscosity, volatility and flammability as alkane chain length increases.
questions.modelAnswer: Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces, requiring more energy to separate: boiling point rises, viscosity rises, volatility falls, ease of ignition generally falls. Covalent bonds are not broken in boiling.
markingPoints: Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces, requiring more energy to separate: boiling point rises, viscosity rises, volatility falls, ease of ignition generally falls. Covalent bonds are not broken in boiling.

questions.questionFamily: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.subtopic: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.question: Write balanced equations for complete combustion of propane and incomplete combustion forming carbon monoxide. Explain one hazard of each incomplete-combustion product.
questions.modelAnswer: C3H8+5O2->3CO2+4H2O; 2C3H8+7O2->6CO+8H2O. CO toxic/reduces oxygen transport; soot particulates damage lungs/global dimming.
markingPoints: 2C3H8+7O2->6CO+8H2O. CO toxic/reduces oxygen transport
soot particulates damage lungs/global dimming.

questions.questionFamily: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.subtopic: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.question: A refinery has excess long-chain fractions but high demand for petrol and alkene feedstock. Explain cracking, give suitable conditions and identify the useful product types.
questions.modelAnswer: Vaporise long-chain hydrocarbons; high temperature over catalyst or steam cracking; C-C bonds break; shorter alkanes are fuels and alkenes make polymers/chemicals.
markingPoints: Vaporise long-chain hydrocarbons
high temperature over catalyst or steam cracking
C-C bonds break
shorter alkanes are fuels and alkenes make polymers/chemicals.

questions.question: Decane cracks to form ethene and one other hydrocarbon. Deduce the formula and state how bromine water distinguishes the two products.
questions.modelAnswer: C10H22 -> C2H4 + C8H18. Ethene decolourises orange bromine water; octane does not under test conditions.
markingPoints: C10H22 -> C2H4 + C8H18. Ethene decolourises orange bromine water

questions.questionFamily: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.subtopic: Carbon Compounds as Fuels and Feedstock
questions.question: Compare complete and incomplete combustion in terms of oxygen supply, products, energy release and environmental effects.
questions.modelAnswer: Plentiful O2 gives CO2+H2O and more complete energy transfer. Limited O2 gives CO and/or carbon+H2O and less energy. CO toxic, soot respiratory/global dimming, CO2 greenhouse gas.
markingPoints: Plentiful O2 gives CO2+H2O and more complete energy transfer. Limited O2 gives CO and/or carbon+H2O and less energy. CO toxic, soot respiratory/global dimming, CO2 greenhouse gas.

questions.questionFamily: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.subtopic: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.question: Ethene reacts separately with hydrogen, steam and bromine. Name the product type/product and state the common reaction feature.
questions.modelAnswer: Hydrogen -> ethane (Ni catalyst); steam -> ethanol (phosphoric acid catalyst); bromine -> dibromoethane. Addition across C=C; double bond opens and one product forms.
markingPoints: Hydrogen -> ethane (Ni catalyst)
steam -> ethanol (phosphoric acid catalyst)
bromine -> dibromoethane. Addition across C=C
double bond opens and one product forms.

questions.questionFamily: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.subtopic: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.question: Compare ethanol manufacture by fermentation and hydration of ethene, including raw materials, conditions, rate, purity, energy, continuity and sustainability.
questions.modelAnswer: Fermentation: renewable sugar, yeast, anaerobic 30-40 C, slow/batch, dilute ethanol needs distillation. Hydration: ethene+steam, high T/P, catalyst, fast/continuous, purer product, finite crude-oil feedstock, higher energy. Balanced judgement.
markingPoints: Fermentation: renewable sugar, yeast, anaerobic 30-40 C, slow/batch, dilute ethanol needs distillation. Hydration: ethene+steam, high T/P, catalyst, fast/continuous, purer product, finite crude-oil feedstock, higher energy. Balanced judgement.

questions.subtopic: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.question: Explain why carboxylic acids are weak acids and predict their reactions with sodium carbonate and an alcohol.
questions.modelAnswer: Partially ionise so lower H+ concentration than equal-concentration strong acid. With carbonate: salt+water+CO2/effervescence. With alcohol: ester+water, acid catalyst/heat.
markingPoints: Partially ionise so lower H+ concentration than equal-concentration strong acid. With carbonate: salt+water+CO2/effervescence. With alcohol: ester+water, acid catalyst/heat.

questions.modelAnswer: Many propene monomers; C=C opens to C-C; no atoms lost; repeating unit [-CH2-CH(CH3)-]n with brackets, continuation bonds and n.

questions.questionFamily: Synthetic and Naturally Occurring Polymers
questions.subtopic: Synthetic and Naturally Occurring Polymers
questions.question: Compare addition and condensation polymerisation, including monomers, products and whether a small molecule forms.
questions.modelAnswer: Addition: unsaturated alkene monomers, one polymer product, no small molecule. Condensation: monomers with two functional groups, polymer plus small molecule such as water; may use two monomer types.
markingPoints: Addition: unsaturated alkene monomers, one polymer product, no small molecule. Condensation: monomers with two functional groups, polymer plus small molecule such as water
may use two monomer types.

questions.question: Explain how a diol and dicarboxylic acid form a polyester and how amino acids form polypeptides.
questions.modelAnswer: Functional groups react repeatedly; ester links form with water eliminated. Amino and carboxyl groups on amino acids react to form peptide links with water eliminated; long chain/polypeptide.
markingPoints: Functional groups react repeatedly
ester links form with water eliminated. Amino and carboxyl groups on amino acids react to form peptide links with water eliminated
long chain/polypeptide.

questions.modelAnswer: Fractions burn to release energy; molecules are starting materials for polymers/solvents/detergents. Finite, environmental impacts/CO2, and higher-value chemical uses support conservation.

questions.question: Write the balanced equation for complete combustion of propane and explain why incomplete combustion is dangerous.

markingPoints: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. Limited oxygen can form carbon monoxide, which binds to haemoglobin and reduces oxygen transport

questions.question: Compare fermentation and hydration for manufacturing ethanol.
questions.modelAnswer: Fermentation uses renewable sugar, low temperature/pressure but is slow, batch, makes dilute impure ethanol and needs distillation. Hydration uses ethene from crude oil, high temperature/pressure and catalyst but is fast, continuous and makes purer ethanol. Choice depends on feedstock, energy and scale.
markingPoints: Fermentation uses renewable sugar, low temperature/pressure but is slow, batch, makes dilute impure ethanol and needs distillation. Hydration uses ethene from crude oil, high temperature/pressure and catalyst but is fast, continuous and makes purer ethanol. Choice depends on feedstock, energy and scale.

questions.question: Explain why bromine-water decolourisation alone does not identify which alkene is present.
questions.modelAnswer: Many alkenes contain a C=C bond and give the same positive result. The test identifies unsaturation, not a unique molecular identity; further analytical evidence is needed.
markingPoints: Many alkenes contain a C=C bond and give the same positive result. The test identifies unsaturation, not a unique molecular identity

questions.questionFamily: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.subtopic: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.question: Compare how yield, rate, purity and energy use should be considered when evaluating fermentation and hydration routes to ethanol.
questions.modelAnswer: Fermentation uses renewable sugars and lower temperature but is slow, produces dilute ethanol and needs purification. Hydration is fast and continuous and produces purer ethanol but uses high temperature/pressure and non-renewable ethene. A conclusion depends on weighted criteria and data.
markingPoints: Fermentation uses renewable sugars and lower temperature but is slow, produces dilute ethanol and needs purification. Hydration is fast and continuous and produces purer ethanol but uses high temperature/pressure and non-renewable ethene. A conclusion depends on weighted criteria and data.

questions.questionFamily: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.subtopic: Reactions of Organic Compounds
questions.question: Explain why a distillation temperature that rises during collection suggests the sample is a mixture rather than a pure liquid.
questions.modelAnswer: A pure liquid boils at a sharp, constant temperature at fixed pressure. A mixture contains components with different boiling points, so vapour composition and temperature change during distillation.
markingPoints: A pure liquid boils at a sharp, constant temperature at fixed pressure. A mixture contains components with different boiling points, so vapour composition and temperature change during distillation.
